refutation_attempt: Read Json.hpp for any depth counter, limit or iterative path (none); checked every ParseJson/ParseCnjEnvelope caller for a size or depth guard before it (none), and TryReadJsonFile catches only JsonParseException. Could not re-run the probe (no builds allowed).
reason: ParseValue/ParseObject/ParseArray recurse per nesting level with no ceiling, so a small crafted .cnj or store file overflows the stack instead of throwing JsonParseException. Confirmed by reading; the entry's g++ probe (100,000 levels, SIGSEGV) was not re-executed here.

refutation_attempt: Grepped every maxFileSize consumer: only the two decompressors and the build-time canonical read use it; ContentReader has no file-size check. Read TryReadAssetBytes, LoadXnbAsset, LoadXnbAssetUntyped, ReadStreamToEnd, ScanXnbReaderNames: bounds are INT32_MAX or none. No test loads an oversized xnb.
reason: An uncompressed .xnb between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is read whole by ContentManager although XnbReadLimits documents maxFileSize as the largest file the reader will open; the manifest scan has no bound at all. Compressed files are bounded by the decompressors. Low severity fits.

refutation_attempt: Looked for deliberate design: tests and plan_xnb keep cache and wrapper lifetime separate, and the C API docs say Unload never releases issued handles. But ReadAsset's header says the manager records disposables itself, ContentReader's fallback is an admitted no-op, and XNA IL disposes on Unload.
reason: Unload() is loadedAssets_.clear(); no disposable is ever recorded, so a copy the game still holds stays undisposed, unlike XNA (decompiled Unload disposes each tracked asset). The ReadAsset header promise of manager-side recording is untrue at TARGET. Design intent is partly deliberate, but the documented contract is broken.

refutation_attempt: Checked decompiled XNA ReadTypeManifest (exact version check) and ReflectiveReader (TypeVersion from the attribute). Read the whole ReflectiveTypeReader header: no version field, no override; SupportsVersion is strict. Considered gap, but the xnb support doc says original implicit-reflective payloads read directly.
reason: A reflective reader always reports version 0 and the builder cannot declare another, so an XNA asset whose type carries [ContentSerializerTypeVersion(2)] fails with an unsupported-version ContentLoadException. Narrowing to the reflective route is right; the built-in half is XNA-faithful. Borderline gap-vs-bug; kept bug because CNA docs promise this payload loads.

refutation_attempt: Searched for chdir, SetCurrentDirectory or any TitleLocation/GetBasePath use in content or Game: none; Game's Content_ is a plain relative root. Verified SDL3 GetBasePath is the exe directory, StandardFileSystem returns current_path, TitleContainer combines with TitleLocation, and docs/apple-platforms.md claims SDL_GetBasePath.
reason: A relative RootDirectory resolves against the process working directory in every tier, while XNA and CNA's own TitleContainer resolve against the title location. Content is missed when launched from another directory, and on Android the .cnb and loose tiers use std::filesystem. Not executed; Apple leg unchecked.

refutation_attempt: Looked for any lock, thread_local or read-only discipline: TypeCreators and TargetTypeNames are plain function-local maps, AssociateTargetType assigns on every reader construction, InitializeTypeReaders constructs readers per file. Checked which renderers implement the context lease: only EasyGL and OpenGL4, and only with a direct device pointer.
reason: Every ContentTypeReader constructor writes the unlocked process-wide TargetTypeNames map on each .xnb load, so two XNB loads on different threads race unless a GL lease happens to serialise them; XNA locks nameToReader. Not provoked, no TSan run; medium is defensible given XNA-style threaded loading.

refutation_attempt: Compared LoadXnbAsset and LoadXnbAssetUntyped side by side; ParseXnbHeader has no hidden length guard; the MemoryStream pointer ctor copies buffer..buffer+size (read in sharp-runtime); untyped Lz4 case throws while typed decodes it; confirmed sole caller is ExternalReferenceReader via ReadExternalReference().
reason: The untyped decoder lacks the compressed totalLength<14 guard, so a 10-13 byte compressed file makes MemoryStream(bytes+10,4) read up to 4 bytes past the vector before the negative size is refused; it also refuses LZ4 that the typed path decodes. Reached only via EffectMaterial external references; heap over-read is tiny, medium is generous.

refutation_attempt: Looked for compensation: Load<T> reads via TryReadAssetBytes; ReadAsset is protected and only tests reach it; nothing public reads the resource family. plan_missing calls the unchanged .xnb tier deliberate, yet the comments say every load uses OpenStream. XNA IL: Load, ReadAsset, OpenStream.
reason: ContentManager::Load<T> never calls the virtual OpenStream, so a derived or ResourceContentManager never serves a public Load<T>; it searches the working directory and throws. The OpenStream and class comments claim otherwise; behaviour was recorded as deliberate in a plan, so the header is wrong or the code is. Bug either way.

refutation_attempt: Traced all three: the xnb tier has no catch around InnerReadObject's any_cast; Load<SoundEffect> returns reader.Read unwrapped and SoundEffect(string) throws NotSupportedException; disposed Load throws runtime_error. Checked XNA IL (BadXnbWrongType, ObjectDisposedException) and the fuzz test accepting bad_any_cast.
reason: Re-derived: Load<Texture2D> of a sound .xnb throws std::bad_any_cast, Load<SoundEffect> of a missing file throws System::NotSupportedException, and a disposed manager throws std::runtime_error. Header promises ContentLoadException, the cnb tier converts bad_any_cast, and XNA throws ContentLoadException or ObjectDisposedException.

refutation_attempt: Looked for an in-progress set, load-depth counter or cache placeholder in ContentManager, ContentReader and the EffectMaterial reader: none; each level builds a fresh ContentReader at depth 0. Confirmed EffectMaterialReader reads its effect via ReadExternalReference, which calls Load. No cycle test exists.
reason: Load<T> and LoadUntypedXnbReference cache only after a successful load, so A referencing B referencing A (or itself) recurses until stack overflow. XNA does the same, so the defect rests on CNA's own hardening comments calling unbounded attacker-driven recursion a bug class. Low severity right.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether Load<T> keeps the reader alive: it binds a reference through a raw pointer into the any, no shared_ptr copy. RegisterTypeReader assigns a new shared_ptr into the same slot, releasing the only owner. RegisterCnjLoader cannot re-register an existing type. No test cited.
reason: A LooseFileContentTypeReader that registers a reader for its own T during Read destroys the executing reader; it runs on freed memory if it touches members afterwards. The entry's example only returns a parameter, so it is a delete-this hazard, not a certain use-after-free. Trigger is application code only; low fits.

refutation_attempt: Looked for an in-loop size check or decoder-side cap: the loop runs while compressed input remains, each block writes up to 64 KiB into a growable MemoryStream, and only the final position is compared; the stream stops at INT32_MAX. LZ4 allocates the declared size.
reason: DecompressXnbPayload validates the declared size, then decodes unbounded and compares once after the loop, so a crafted LZX stream within the 64 MiB file cap can allocate up to about 2 GiB against a documented 256 MiB maxDecompressedSize. Achievable ratio not measured; only hostile files affected.

refutation_attempt: Grepped objectNestingDepth_ and maxObjectNestingDepth: only InnerReadObject<T> touches them. InnerReadObjectAny has no guard, StringObjectDictionaryReader reads values with the untyped ReadObject(), and its typed key read enters and leaves the guard before recursing, so the counter never rises. ReadUntyped adds no limit.
reason: Nested Dictionary<String,Object> values (also Model tags, shared resources, untyped roots) recurse through the unguarded untyped path, so a small crafted .xnb overflows the stack instead of throwing at maxObjectNestingDepth. Typed graphs are bounded and tested; the untyped path is not.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a zero-bone guard in Model::Draw and for a rule forbidding zero-bone models: the constructor and ModelTests build them, and getBoundingSphereEXTProperty explicitly handles boneCount 0 with identity, but Draw indexes sharedDrawBoneMatrices_[0] unchecked. XNA has no public Model constructor.
reason: A hand-built zero-bone model with a parentless mesh and an IEffectMatrices effect makes Draw read sharedDrawBoneMatrices_[0] from an empty or stale thread-local vector. The constructor, its 'leniency' comment and the bounding-sphere code all treat zero bones as valid. Content-loaded models always have a root bone.

refutation_attempt: Read BlendMorphTargetsEXT for any size check beyond the weight count: NormalDeltas[t] and the per-vertex PositionDeltas/NormalDeltas indexing are unguarded, only TangentDeltas has a bounds test. Checked that the .cnj morph reader and glTF importer build consistent arrays, so only hand-built data reaches it.
reason: With a MorphTargetDataEXT whose NormalDeltas is shorter than PositionDeltas, or whose non-empty delta arrays hold fewer entries than the vertex count, the blend reads out of range for any non-zero weight. Field docs imply per-target entries but no check exists. Imported data is validated; low fits.

refutation_attempt: Compared the Model and SkinnedModel readers: SkinnedModel also skips when vertexStride <= 0, so the stride skip is shared. The Task 11.9 size-multiple and index-range checks exist only there; the shared builder truncates by division and never range-checks indices.
reason: Real, but the summary implies the SkinnedModel reader throws for a non-positive stride; it silently skips too. The genuine divergence is size truncation and missing index-range validation in the Model path (Task 11.9 checks only exist in the SkinnedModel reader). Wording corrected accordingly.

correction.title: The .cnj Model reader truncates vertex and index sidecar sizes and never range-checks indices, where the SkinnedModel reader refuses the same input
correction.summary: ModelTypeReader and BuildModelMeshPartGeometryEXT derive vertex and index counts by integer division, discarding trailing bytes, and build the index buffer without checking indices against the vertex count; the SkinnedModel reader in the same file throws ContentLoadException for both. A mesh with a non-positive vertexStride is silently skipped, as it is in the SkinnedModel reader.
correction.expected: A malformed Model descriptor should be refused with ContentLoadException. The same file's SkinnedModel reader does this deliberately (Task 11.9): it throws when the vertex data is not a multiple of vertexStride or the index data not a multiple of the index size, and checks every index against the vertex count.
correction.actual: In modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp the Model reader's mesh loop computes numVertices = size / stride, and BuildModelMeshPartGeometryEXT divides the vertex and index byte counts likewise, dropping any remainder, and builds the index buffer without checking indices against the vertex count, so a corrupt sidecar yields a truncated mesh or indices that reference missing vertices. Both the Model and SkinnedModel readers silently skip a mesh whose vertexStride is zero or negative (and one with no vertices or indices file); that skip is not a divergence between them.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. Correction: the original wording listed the stride skip as something the SkinnedModel reader refuses; it does not, both use `continue`.

read: modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp::ModelTypeReader mesh loop (stride <= 0 continue, numVertices by division)

refutation_attempt: Read the bone loop: parent is only range-checked against the full bone count, so a forward or self parent passes; AddChild has no guard; a transform without exactly 16 numbers stays identity. AnimationPlayer throws for unordered hierarchies, Model has no such check.
reason: A .cnj Model bones array may name a later bone or itself as parent and pass the range check, so CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo composes against an uncomputed slot; a transform without exactly 16 numbers becomes identity silently. cnj format comments promise parent-before-child order; nothing enforces it. Hand-authored files only.

refutation_attempt: Compared with decompiled XNA DateTimeReader (restores kind and converts Local via ToLocalTime) and tested the stated cause: a CNA content-pipeline test constructs System::DateTime(ticks, System::DateTimeKind::Utc), and sharp-runtime has stored a kind since 2026-08-19, so the header's 'no kind' premise is stale.
reason: The reader does discard the kind bits and the header calls it a deviation, so it is a documented gap. But the stated cause is wrong at TARGET: System::DateTime has a (ticks, DateTimeKind) constructor. Also XNA converts Local values to local time, which CNA does not do, so the value differs, not only the kind.

correction.summary: DateTimeReader masks off the two kind bits and returns System::DateTime(ticks) with an unspecified kind, and it does not convert a Local-kind value to local time as XNA does. The header justifies the deviation by System::DateTime not modelling a kind, but System::DateTime has a (ticks, DateTimeKind) constructor at TARGET, so that reason is stale.
correction.expected: XNA's DateTimeReader restores DateTimeKind from the top two bits and, for a Local value, converts the stored UTC ticks to local time (new DateTime(ticks, Utc).ToLocalTime()).
correction.actual: modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Xnb/DecimalDateTimeContentTypeReaders.hpp applies kindMask = 3 << 62 and returns System::DateTime(ticks). Its comment documents this as a deliberate deviation because System::DateTime 'does not store/track DateTimeKind at all'; that premise is out of date, since CNA's own XnaIntermediateSerializerTests builds Utc values with System::DateTime(ticks, System::DateTimeKind::Utc). The XNB writer in modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbBuiltInWriters.cpp likewise writes Unspecified. A Local-kind value therefore loads as its stored UTC ticks, without XNA's offset conversion.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. XNA behaviour from the decompiled DateTimeReader. sharp-runtime's DateTime kind storage (packed in the top two bits, ticket 1941) landed on 2026-08-19, before the TARGET commit, and was read there through git only.

refutation_attempt: Grepped every setCamerasEXTProperty caller (one, in the runtime glTF reader), camera handling in the .cnj Model reader, the cnb codecs and both converter tools (only cameraNodeCount in the gltf_to_cnj report). Model.hpp documents the property as empty for every other content path.
reason: Only the direct glTF route fills Model::CamerasEXT; the .cnj/.cnb routes carry no camera data, and the header says so. Documented incompleteness rather than a contract violation, so a functional gap fits. gltf_to_cnb delegates to the cnj output.

refutation_attempt: Checked every extraction call in ReadGltfModel for a scale source (all pass 1.0f, comment records the limit) and read both converter CLIs: gltf_to_cnb has --unit-scale, but gltf_to_cnj takes an optional positional unitScale argument, not that flag. No runtime load-options object exists.
reason: The runtime glTF path really has no unit scale, and its own comment documents that, so it is a functional gap. One detail is wrong: gltf_to_cnj does not accept --unit-scale; it takes a fourth positional unitScale argument. The entry names no test, though the tool tests cover offline scaling.

correction.summary: ContentManager's glTF reader always imports at unitScale 1.0, so a file not authored in metres must go through the offline converters: cna_tool_gltf_to_cnb --unit-scale, or the optional unitScale argument of cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj.
correction.actual: The runtime reader in modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp passes 1.0f to every extraction step, and its own comment records the limit: "unitScale is always 1.0 (no CLI-argument equivalent exists for runtime loading); a source file not authored in meters needs the offline tool instead." tools/gltf_to_cnb/gltf_to_cnb.cpp accepts --unit-scale <f>; tools/gltf_to_cnj/gltf_to_cnj.cpp takes an optional fourth positional argument, unitScale.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. Correction: the original text said both tools accept --unit-scale; only gltf_to_cnb does. Workaround wording: convert with gltf_to_cnb --unit-scale or gltf_to_cnj's positional unitScale, or apply a scale to the world matrix when drawing. Offline scaling is exercised by modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/GltfToCnjToolTests.cpp.

refutation_attempt: Looked for instancing support or a silent path: the extension registry row is Unsupported, ReadGltfModel warns per file, AppendGltfNodeGraphReportEXT emits gpu-instancing-dropped, and docs/gltf-limitations.md lists it (rows and section 4.1). No refusal or contract promises reproduction.

refutation_attempt: Checked the hinted duplicate: read CNA-BUG-243 (docs row says CNA reverses winding) against the code, which warns per mirrored placement and reports mirrored-winding-unapplied; also grepped Model, ModelMesh and ModelMeshPart headers for any mirror flag or cull hook (none).
reason: Mirrored placements keep shared winding by design, documented in code, report and tests; no property exposes the flag. Not a duplicate of CNA-BUG-243: that entry is the stale doc row claiming reversal, this is the missing behaviour that row falsely promises, and the two should stay linked.

refutation_attempt: Looked for silent loss or a wrong diagnostic name: AppendGltfMeshReportEXT emits uv-set-mismatch, influence-sets-dropped and color-sets-dropped, and docs/gltf-limitations.md rows 116 and 121 name the same report fields (GLTF-091, GLTF-188). Nothing promises more than two UV channels, one colour set or one influence set.
reason: The packed vertex ABI carries two UV channels, one joint-influence set and one colour set; further sets are dropped and reported by name, as the limitations document states. Documented, reported, non-silent limit, so a functional gap fits.

refutation_attempt: Traced ReadGltfModel: the skinned branch counts scene-node tracks not carried by any retained skin, appends the rigid-animation-dropped diagnostic and warns; only the unskinned branch builds ModelAnimationsEXT. CountGltfRigidAnimationDropsEXT keeps tracks on skin joints. Model::Tag limitation is recorded as GLTF-295.
reason: A skinned glTF model keeps only skin-carried tracks; rigid scene-node clips on non-joint nodes are dropped and reported because Model::Tag already holds SkinningData. Deliberate, recorded and reported, so a functional gap.

refutation_attempt: Read ExtractMorphWeightTrack: it takes the first node in file order whose mesh matches and reads only channels targeting that node, returning the first matching channel. Checked the header doc calling this a documented simplification, and that default weights are read per instancing node via GetMeshDefaultWeights.
reason: A morphed mesh instanced by several nodes plays the first node's weights channel on every placement; other nodes' channels are ignored. Documented simplification, contrast with per-node default weights confirmed. Functional gap is right; it also returns only the first weights channel found across animations.

refutation_attempt: Read BuildTrack (union of channel key times, per-time channel evaluation) and AnimationPlayer's SampleTrack (Vector3::Lerp and Quaternion::Slerp between keys, no tangents). Checked the limitations row quoting piecewise-linear/spherical and the 9.6 percent fixture error, and that morph-weight tracks keep tangents.
reason: Bone and node CUBICSPLINE channels are baked at union key times and played back with lerp/slerp, so the curve between keys is lost. The limitation and the measured error are documented by CNA. Functional gap fits; the 9.6 percent figure is CNA's own fixture measurement, not re-run.

refutation_attempt: Read BuildSkeleton: it throws when joints exceed 72, naming skin, count and limit, before any truncation. Confirmed SkinnedEffect::MaxBones is 72 and the XNA spec documents 72 as the maximum. Found a dedicated test (73-joint fixture refused) beyond the probe the entry cites.
reason: A glTF skin above 72 joints is refused at import, a deliberate documented choice over truncation that would collapse vertices; the 72 limit is XNA's own. Nothing promises larger rigs, so a functional gap fits.

refutation_attempt: Read ExtractPunctualLightsEXT: it caps at three lights and counts the rest, turns point and spot into directional lights aimed at the origin, counts ignored range and cone, and clamps intensity. Checked the limitations row (APPROXIMATED_AND_REPORTED) and plan_gltf GLTF-459 row 6.
reason: KHR_lights_punctual is mapped onto XNA's three directional lights: extra lights dropped, point and spot approximated, range and cone ignored, every loss counted in the import report. Documented in code, docs and plan; XNA's IEffectLights cannot express more. Functional gap fits.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the arithmetic (AlphaBlend is One/InverseSourceAlpha, keyed texel is (key,0)). But plan_cnj CNB-9 defines the behaviour as 'become transparent (alpha 0)', CnjSourceFileTests pins Color(255,0,255,0), the pipeline comment says an authored key keeps its colour, and no CNA doc promises invisibility for straight-alpha textures.
reason: The (key RGB, alpha 0) texel is deliberate, plan-defined and test-pinned, and loose-tier textures are straight alpha everywhere; the additive tint under default AlphaBlend is a real caveat but no contract is violated. The suggested (0,0,0,0) fix would contradict an existing test. A gap fits better than a bug.

correction.title: A runtime .cnj Texture2D colorKey leaves keyed texels as straight-alpha (key RGB, alpha 0), so they are invisible only under a non-premultiplied blend state
correction.summary: The loose-tier .cnj Texture2D reader writes Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0) into a straight-alpha texture, deliberately: plans/plan_cnj.md CNB-9 defines the result as transparent with alpha 0, and CnjSourceFileTests pins it. Under SpriteBatch's default premultiplied AlphaBlend such a texel adds the key colour instead of vanishing; the compiled route premultiplies after keying and clears it.
correction.expected: A colour-keyed texel is not visible when the texture is drawn with SpriteBatch::Begin()'s default blend state, as it is when the same document is compiled to .cnb.
correction.actual: ApplyColorKey in modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp replaces each matching texel with Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0) and does not premultiply; the texture is straight alpha like every loose-loaded image. BlendState::AlphaBlend (One, InverseSourceAlpha) then adds the key colour to the destination inside the sprite's rectangle. BlendState::NonPremultiplied hides the texel. The pipeline comment in modules/content/src/Pipeline/Texture2DContentPipeline.cpp records that an authored key keeps its colour on purpose.
correction.evidence_note: Read at 009d40f5; not executed. The original entry omitted modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/CnjSourceFileTests.cpp (ColorKeyMakesMatchingPixelsTransparentOthersUnchanged), which asserts Color(255, 0, 255, 0) for keyed pixels, and plans/plan_cnj.md CNB-9, which specifies 'magenta pixels become transparent (alpha 0)'. Writing Color(0,0,0,0) in ApplyColorKey would need that test changed. No CNA document promises invisibility under the default blend state for runtime-loaded straight-alpha textures.
